newsitem.title: USA: U.S. views China offers on WTO entry as inadequate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. views China offers on WTO entry as inadequate.

text.p: The Clinton administration views China's negotiating offers in its effort to join the World Trade Organization (WTO) as inadequate, a U.S. official who asked not to be identified said on Monday.

"The bottom line is we have not seen a substantial change in China's offers this year," said the official. "We are not on a trajectory where either the U.S. or a number of our trading partners would begin to regard China's offers as meeting the conditions necessary for WTO accession."
The U.S. official, who asked not to be identified, said that the United States had a broad range of concerns that needed to be addressed for China to be admitted to the WTO.

"The issues range from market access to transparency in government procurement and business trasactions, to reduction of tariffs and the elimination of non-tariff barriers to trade, to subsidies," he said.

"We have long insisted a good offer will be comprehensive and address concerns in all of these areas," he added, saying the United States was particularly troubled in its most recent round of talks that China did not make offers in the areas of services and agriculture.

The official said no further negotiations were scheduled following the last round of talks, which ended on Friday, but said the administration expects to have an "ongoing dialogue" with China on the matter of its WTO entry.

He also noted that China is expected to make a new offer in September, one month before Chinese President Jiang Zemin is scheduled to visit Washington for a summit meeting with President Bill Clinton.
